answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to hold a stake of verifiable work before it can trade: each agent must lock a deposit tied to a unique vertex in a reputation graph, so spinning up thousands of fake accounts means funding each one. Like basalt foundations under a tundra outpost, the stake is slow to build and costly to abandon, while honest agents earn it back through reliable service — making an attack expensive and one real identity far more valuable than a swarm of cheap copies.
